claims.text: After PCI for stable disease, DAPT (aspirin + clopidogrel, prasugrel or ticagrelor) usually for 12 months.
claims.quote: Dual-antiplatelet therapy is used after percutaneous coronary intervention (for stable disease, or after acute coronary syndrome in previously stable disease), with aspirin and a P2Y12 inhibitor (eg, clopidogrel, prasugrel, ticagrelor) usually for 12 months.

claims.text: for PCI, 300–600 mg PO once, then 75 mg daily for 1–12 months.

claims.text: Ticagrelor: for PCI, 180 mg PO once before the procedure, then 90 mg BID for 1–12 months.
claims.quote: For patients undergoing PCI: 180 mg orally once before the procedure, followed by 90 mg orally twice a day for 1–12 months

claims.text: Morphine and fentanyl may attenuate the activity of some P2Y12 inhibitors and may contribute to worse outcomes.
claims.quote: Although opioids have long been used to treat pain in patients with acute coronary syndromes, data suggest that morphine and fentanyl attenuate activity of some P2Y12 receptor inhibitors and may contribute to worse patient outcomes (3, 4, 5).
